name: Medulance
tagline: App-based ambulance and emergency response network
excerpt: Ambulance network Medulance turned down ₹5 crore and took a ₹2 crore deal from three sharks on Shark Tank India Season 2.
content:
Medulance runs an emergency response network that connects patients with ambulances through an app and helpline, working with private ambulance operators and corporate and hospital clients. It was started in 2017 by Pranav Bajaj and Ravjot Singh Arora.

In Shark Tank India Season 2, Episode 35, the founders asked for ₹2 crore for 1%. The sharks first offered ₹5 crore for 5%. The founders declined and accepted ₹2 crore for 2% from Namita Thapar, Aman Gupta and Peyush Bansal, a ₹100 crore valuation, as reported by Business Standard (ANI). It was the company's first outside funding.

In April 2024 YourStory reported a $3 million Series A led by Alkemi Growth Capital, with Aman Gupta and Namita Thapar participating. In September 2026 Inc42 reported a further ₹24 crore Series A2 round led by Auxano Capital; the company claimed a fleet of more than 15,000 ambulances in over 500 cities. Revenue for recent years has not been reported in the outlets we track.

Medulance shows founders choosing lower dilution over a bigger headline cheque.

faq.q: Did Medulance get a deal on Shark Tank India?
faq.a: Yes. Namita Thapar, Aman Gupta and Peyush Bansal invested ₹2 crore for 2%.

faq.q: Why did Medulance turn down ₹5 crore?
faq.a: The founders preferred less dilution and took ₹2 crore for 2% instead of ₹5 crore for 5%.

faq.q: Has Medulance raised money since Shark Tank?
faq.a: Yes. A $3 million Series A in 2024 and a ₹24 crore Series A2 in 2026.
Recent revenue has not been reported in the outlets we track.

lessons: Bootstrapping to profitability before the show gave the founders leverage to refuse a larger offer.
When sharks follow on in later rounds, it is a strong sign the TV deal turned into a real partnership.
Fleet size claims are company figures; regulators and customers judge response times.
